newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to consolidate once dust settles.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to consolidate once dust settles.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, hit in line with Bunds by a slump in U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday, are expected to consolidate at current levels once the dust has settled, dealers said.
"I don't believe in a steeper correction. The 10-year yield should remain between 5.95 and 6.00 percent to the year-end once markets have calmed down later this week," said Geert Huyghe at CERA.
The benchmark 2006 OLO yielded 5.97 percent after earlier flirting with the 5.99/6.00 percent level. It had been at 5.87 percent at the close on Tuesday.
Traders noted market volatility had increased considerably. "There's no panic, but the market sure is nervous," one said.

Huyghe said the OLO yield curve was steepening as the short end was not affected by the sell-off. The market believed the Bundesbank would keep key short-term interest rates steady, even if selling in the long end continued.
"Which is a good sign. Normally the short end is hit first if a serious correction is in the works. People may be worrying too soon," he said.
The 10-year spread with equivalent German Bunds was at 10 basis points for most of the day, down from 11 on Tuesday. It briefly narrowed to nine basis points shortly before the close.
Traders said they felt comfortable about the current spread and expected it to remain around 10 for the rest of the year.
